summary: A tag is a permanent name for one commit, such as v1.0. Use tags to mark versions you turned in or released.
notes: Unlike a branch, a tag does not move when you make new commits.
git push does not send tags. Use git push origin v1.0 for one tag or git push --tags for all of them.
git switch --detach v1.0 lets you look at the files as they were in that version.
pitfall: git tag v1.0 without -a makes a lightweight tag with no message or date. Use -a and -m for versions you want to describe.
setup_note: Starts in a repository with three commits on main.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Print the highest score"
